warnings: This is a multi-location, multi-year study with 23 site-years across 7 countries - each location-year combination should be treated as a separate experiment
Three different Zn treatments (soil Zn, foliar Zn, soil+foliar Zn) all use the same nil Zn control - extract each treatment separately vs nil Zn
Table 5 contains the primary outcome (grain Zn concentration) - do not confuse with Table 3 (grain yield) or Table 4 (leaf Zn concentration)
Some locations have data for multiple years (2009-2010, 2010-2011) - treat each year as separate observation
Zambia location has 'Nd' (no data) for foliar Zn treatment - only soil and soil+foliar treatments available
LSD values are provided when F-test is significant, otherwise marked as 'Ns' with no LSD
WARNING: VAR-UNCLEAR - Variance type not clearly stated
recon.variance_source: Data from each location were analyzed using one-factor ANOVA process and means were separated by least significance difference (LSD) at P<0.05 level
recon.control_definition: Nil Zn (control) - no zinc fertilizer application
recon.treatment_definition: Three treatments: (1) Soil Zn application (50kg ZnSO4·7H2O ha−1), (2) Foliar Zn application (0.5% ZnSO4·7H2O solution applied twice at heading and milk stages), (3) Soil + foliar Zn application (combination of both)
recon.potential_tc_confusion: None - control clearly defined as 'Nil Zn'
recon.sample_size_source: four Zn treatments including nil Zn (control), soil Zn application, foliar Zn application and soil +foliar Zn application were applied in a completely randomized block design with four to six replications except Zambia
recon.extraction_guidance: Extract from Table 5 only. Each row represents a separate experiment (location-year combination). For each location-year, extract three comparisons: (1) Soil Zn vs Nil, (2) Foliar Zn vs Nil, (3) Soil+foliar Zn vs Nil. Use LSD0.05 values as variance measure when F-test is significant. Skip Zambia foliar treatment (marked as 'Nd'). Grand means at bottom show overall effects but individual location-year data should be extracted for meta-analysis.
